Subject: Capacity + packaging question: tilt toward throughput or feature set?

Hi Irene,

Quick one from our side as we prep the Q3 expansion: our usage spiked in May (attached) and the product team is debating two directions — guarantee more throughput (lower p/token) or keep the higher-tier feature bundle (structured output, tool calling, long-context affordances).

Current situation: 8M tokens/month steady but peaks at 550 rps for short bursts. We added a couple of heavy evals that use the structured output features. The engineering lead thinks Dedicated GPUs make more sense for throughput; product wants the higher-tier feature set.

Questions for Redwood:
- Is there a clean upgrade path that preserves feature parity while giving us predictable throughput?
- Any recommended short-term pilot (3 months) we can do to test Dedicated without full commit?
- How do discounts/credits look if we commit to a 6-month throughput minimum but keep advanced features enabled?

Attaching our May usage export for reference (healthscale_usage_may2028.csv).

Thanks — Samir

Samir — thanks for the data, that’s helpful. High level: there are two pragmatic paths and a hybrid pilot we often use. I'll summarize and then attach an options sheet.

1) Throughput-first (Dedicated)
   - Pros: predictable latency, better cost per token at scale, autoscale pools for burst-to-peak behavior.
   - Cons: feature parity is typically preserved but some advanced integrations (early test builds for structured-output helpers) may live as hosted add-ons initially.

2) Feature-first (Hosted + premium bundle)
   - Pros: immediate access to the latest structured-output and tool-calling features, simpler ops.
   - Cons: unit cost is higher during heavy sustained throughput; burst behavior depends on regional capacity.

3) Hybrid pilot (what I recommend for you)
   - 3-month pilot: reserve a small Dedicated pool sized for your 95th percentile baseline and keep premium bundle enabled on the hosted tier for features that aren't yet migrated to Dedicated kernels. We route production critical traffic to Dedicated; feature-heavy, lower-SLO evals to hosted.
   - Discounting: we can offer a pilot credit (one-time) and a tiered discount on a 6-month committed throughput agreement.

Ben, looping you to outline how discounts and the seat/throughput trade will be modeled (Ben: see suggested pricing sheet attached). I attached a compact options PDF (packaging_options_v1.pdf).

Next steps: can you confirm target 95th percentile rps and whether the structured-output calls are latency-critical? If you're okay, Ben will send a spreadsheet with modeled TCO and a suggested 3-month pilot POC.

— Irene

Samir + team — added fiscal/discount perspective and a concrete proposal in the attached spreadsheet (pricing_matrix_v4.xlsx). Key highlights: 

- Pilot structure (recommended): 3 months, reserved Dedicated pool sized at 60% of your peak (config can be adjusted weekly). We provide $12k in pilot credits toward host-bundled feature calls (so you can keep running structured-output tests on hosted without extra cost during pilot).
- Post-pilot options: a 6-month committed contract with two options:
    A) Throughput-committed: Commit to X tokens/month (we model at your May + 25% headroom). You get a 15% discount on base token rates + lowered ingress fees; structured-output features remain enabled as an add-on at a fixed per-call fee.
    B) Hybrid-commit: Commit to Dedicated baseline and add a premium feature bundle (discounted 10% off list). This aligns engineering ops and maintains feature parity.
- Credits & amortization: We can ladder a one-time onboarding credit and prorate credits against the first 3 invoices.

Marissa — if HealthScale signs the pilot, can you confirm the approval flow and whether we need an SOW or a simple pilot addendum?

Samir — two asks from us to finalize:
1) Confirm the 95th percentile rps target you mentioned (so we size Dedicated correctly).
2) Confirm whether the structured-output calls must hit the same latency SLO as the user-facing text generation (i.e., 250ms tail).

Attaching pricing_matrix_v4.xlsx for modeling.

Thanks,
